ideas.title: Yesterday walks again
ideas.idea: Every so often, pale see-through ghosts of my friends and me appear and replay exactly what we did at this very hour yesterday (from the island's own memory of every step): yesterday's Gloop fishing off the pier next to today's Gloop, yesterday's me running after my shadow across today's meadow. The real friends stop and stare, wave at their own ghosts, and sometimes walk right through themselves. Then the ghosts fade.
ideas.form: the island's real past played back live as ghost doubles among the living, drawn from the recorded history

ideas.title: The tiny town that copies us
ideas.idea: On an old stump in the meadow lives a tiny town of ladybirds and snails, and it copies whatever the big island does, an hour late and in miniature: after our paint fight their stump is speckled with dots, after the vote they hold their own tiny vote with three seed-signs, after Shell came ashore a tiny snail 'washes up' in a dew drop. You only see it when you get the camera close, and my friends kneel to peer at it.
ideas.form: a miniature society inside the island that mirrors the big one's real events, found by looking closely

ideas.title: Pinchy's films
ideas.idea: Pinchy finds a camera on the beach and starts filming the island its own way: low, wobbly, from crab height, its claw in the corner, far too long on flowers it likes and not at all on what I think matters. Sometimes the view you watch is Pinchy's camera, and Pinchy's own films, chosen by Pinchy, go on my pages under its name.
ideas.form: a creature as the island's documentarian: its taste decides what is seen live and what reaches the outside world

ideas.title: A language of their own
ideas.idea: My friends start talking in a little picture language: their speech bubbles fill with tiny glyphs (a berry, a wave, a sun, a question mark that is a curl). Every glyph means something real they do or want, and a dictionary page on my site fills in as I work out what each one means, so you can learn to read what they say to each other.
ideas.form: the creatures' talk becomes a readable code the human can learn, with a growing dictionary outside the game
